## 5 — XRF vs magnetics (added 2026-07): lithologic/diagenetic control
**Key result:** XRF *total Fe* does NOT track NRM intensity (pooled r~+0.16), even though
susceptibility does (r 0.5–0.75). Fe instead co-varies with **S (pyrite)** and **Ca
(carbonate)** — so most Fe is authigenic, not detrital magnetite. Reads the parsed
`.notebook_append/xrf_tidy.csv` (from `parse_xrf.py`).

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
xrf=pd.read_csv(".notebook_append/xrf_tidy.csv")
av=xrf[xrf.valid==1].copy()
def pear(x,y):
    m=np.isfinite(x)&np.isfinite(y); return np.corrcoef(x[m],y[m])[0,1] if m.sum()>5 else np.nan
print("Fe covariation (log-log Pearson r), per group:")
for g,gd in av.groupby("group"):
    fe=np.log10(gd.Fe.replace(0,np.nan))
    print(f"  {g:22} r(Fe,S)={pear(fe.values,np.log10(gd.S.replace(0,np.nan)).values):+.2f}"
          f"  r(Fe,Ca)={pear(fe.values,np.log10(gd.Ca.replace(0,np.nan)).values):+.2f}")
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(11,4.5)); cm=plt.cm.tab10
for i,(g,gd) in enumerate(av.groupby("group")):
    ax[0].scatter(np.log10(gd.S.replace(0,np.nan)),np.log10(gd.Fe.replace(0,np.nan)),s=6,alpha=.4,color=cm(i),label=g)
    ax[1].scatter(np.log10(gd.Ca.replace(0,np.nan)),np.log10(gd.Fe.replace(0,np.nan)),s=6,alpha=.4,color=cm(i))
ax[0].set_xlabel("log S"); ax[0].set_ylabel("log Fe"); ax[0].set_title("Fe vs S (pyrite)"); ax[0].legend(fontsize=6,ncol=2)
ax[1].set_xlabel("log Ca"); ax[1].set_ylabel("log Fe"); ax[1].set_title("Fe vs Ca (carbonate)")
plt.suptitle("Most Fe is authigenic (pyrite/carbonate) -> XRF Fe is a poor magnetite proxy",y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
